Communication

Mobile app and website · UX/UI, branding, research

An app and website that helps people with hearing and speech difficulties communicate. It translates sign language into text or voice, and adds training, progress tracking and specialist support so users can build skills and reach therapy goals.

The problemPeople with hearing and speech difficulties often have no single place to practice, track progress and reach specialists.
The solutionOne platform with sign language translation, guided daily training, psychological support and a record of each user’s medical journey.
Who it’s forUsers with hearing or speech difficulties, their trainers and specialists, and the wider community.

Key features

Real-time translationSign language turned into text or voice.
Interactive trainingDaily plans (Day 1, Day 2, Day 3) with modules for communication, listening, speaking, reading and writing.
Progress trackingA progress ring and sliders that show improvement over time.
Specialist chat and reviewsTrainer profiles, user reviews with star ratings, and notes and tasks.
Medical profileMedical history, disease assessment, treatment plans and treatment progress in one record.
Community awarenessA community section that helps raise awareness about hearing and speech challenges.

Design approach

LayoutClean and user-centric: a top navigation bar for Home, Training and Profile, card-based sections, large accessible buttons and clear icons.
Color paletteTeal, peach, navy blue and gray, chosen to feel professional, calm and inclusive.
LogoA speech bubble combined with sound waves, which represents interaction and accessibility.

Research and inspiration

  • Speech Blubs
  • Lingraphica
  • Khan Academy Kids
  • Google Speech-to-Text
  • Calm
  • Positive reinforcement theory

Design process

  • Empathy

  • Idea
  • Vision
  • Prototype
  • Testing

ECHO: Warzone Rising

Game concept · Pitch design, world and character direction

A tactical first-person shooter set in a war-torn futuristic world where a rogue AI has taken over major cities. Players are elite operatives who reclaim lost zones and uncover where the AI uprising began, across destructible urban and industrial battlefields.

GenreTactical first-person shooter with story missions and multiplayer modes.
Inspired byModern Warfare II for tactical combat, Titanfall 2 for mech warfare, The Division 2 for gritty cooperative environments.
GoalComplete missions to reclaim cities from the rogue AI and defeat towering mechs.
ChallengeSurvive adaptive AI enemies and endless combat waves.
  • Squad playFight as a team, not alone.
  • Intel before actionDrones give real-time information before the fight starts.
  • Destructible spacesCover and routes change during a firefight.

How it plays

Squad playCoordinate roles and positions with your team.
Drone intelScout first with drones, then decide how to engage.
Destructible environmentsShatter walls and panels, and re-read cover and routes as they change.
Infantry firefightsAim, move and use cover precisely.
AI mechsChange tactics for much larger threats.
Select mapThree battlefields in the map menu: ruined city, red zone and frozen territory.

World and look

Warm metalRust-red and orange interiors feel heavy, industrial and military.
Cold accentsCyan and blue lights give the rogue AI a visible presence inside the space.
Layered spacesCatwalks, pipes and grates create lines of sight, ledges and flanking routes.
Readable squadOperatives differ in headgear, colour and build so teammates are easy to tell apart in a fight.

Design goals

  • Reward information over speed
  • Keep the space alive with destruction
  • Alternate small infantry fights with large mech battles
